newsitem.title: KENYA: Rebel Zairean radio says 700 troops killed.
newsitem.headline: Rebel Zairean radio says 700 troops killed.

text.p: Zairean rebel radio said on Tuesday 700 government troops were killed in fighting on Sunday around a key bridge over the Oso river near the eastern town of Walikale.
Rebel Radio of the People, in the rebel-held eastern town of Bukavu and monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, gave no details and there was no independent confirmation.

But Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila denied on Monday a Zairean government announcement that its troops last week had recaptured Walikale, some 120 km (80 miles) from rebel headquarters in the city of Goma, and had killed 100 rebels.

Kabila told the BBC the rebels had had no trouble from the counter-offensive announced by Kinshasa. He said foreign mercenaries had stopped fighting and resumed training after two were killed by rebels.

He denied Walikale had fallen and said the government report of its capture was meant to fool Zaireans. Kabila said the government campaign would fail to recover eastern Zaire from rebels because the Zairean army was ineffective and mercenaries wanted to live to spend their salaries.

Paul Kageme, Rwanda's military strongman said on Tuesday he was concerned at the counter-offensive and hoped it would not spill into Rwanda. Vice-President and Defence Minister Paul Kagame however said the rebels currently appeared to be winning.

"We are taking seriously the possibility of a counter- offensive by the Zaireans and of course we want to keep this outside Rwanda," Kagame, Rwanda's former Tutsi rebel leader, told reporters at Kigali airport.
"But at the moment it appears this is a fight the rebels are winning and the Zaireans seem to be more talk than action on the ground as events are showing," he added.
The Rwandan-backed rebels seized territory bordering Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi starting in October. Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko has vowed the army will crush them.

Witnesses said the shrouded body of a white mercenary killed fighting rebels arrived by helicopter over the weekend in Kisangani, headquarters for the government counter-offensive. Up to 300 soldiers of fortune, many Serbs from the former Yugoslavia, are in east Zaire to help the government.
